recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No source change is needed for FHIR-19468; restoring not-taken to status or adding another taken/not-taken element would conflict with later Pharmacy decisions that keep adherence as the computable representation.
issue_request: FHIR-19468 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification Pharmacy change request for R5 asking whether taken/not-taken needed to be restored to MedicationStatement. The approved resolution was to remove not-taken from MedicationUsage.status and add/use the adherence attribute from FHIR-19470 for taken/not-taken information.
initial_application: Commit f351511a95 applied the FHIR-19468/FHIR-19470/FHIR-28593 change family by removing not-taken status semantics from MedicationUsage.status, making status describe the recording state, and adding MedicationUsage.adherence plus adherence terminology and examples.
additional_context: FHIR-19470 supplied the paired adherence rename/addition and is already represented on the combined branch by 8912f00eea, which fixed the remaining stale takenAsOrdered search-parameter path metadata. FHIR-28593, FHIR-32060, and FHIR-39271 later refined or reaffirmed the split between statement-record status and adherence-based taking/not-taking semantics. FHIR-38682 renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while retaining those status/adherence changes.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active MedicationStatement resource has status bound to recorded | entered-in-error | draft, explicitly directs taking/not-taking users to MedicationStatement.adherence, defines the adherence backbone, and includes the not-taking adherence code.

related_jiras.note: Paired Published/Persuasive issue adding and renaming the adherence attribute used to carry taking/not-taking semantics; already represented on the combined branch.
Confirmed MedicationUsage.status should describe record status rather than clinical usage state.
Refined the status code set to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft.
Renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement while keeping the adherence/status model.
Later Pharmacy decision explicitly reaffirming that adherence, not status, reflects whether medication is being taken.
